title.narrative: Ghana: Energy Development and Access Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Energy Development and Access Project in Ghana is to improve the operational efficiency of the electricity distribution system and increase the population's access to electricity. This will also cause Ghana to support its transition to a low-carbon economy through the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (GHG). The project has three main components: (a) sector and institutional development, which will through technical assistance, capacity-building, and studies, will strengthen the capacity of key institutions participating in the project ; (b) distribution improvement, which involves the construction of eight new 33/11 kV substations along with the feeders; the construction and strengthening of bulk supply points; and upgrading of existing substations in several targeted distribution areas; and (c) electricity access and renewable energy, which involves the set up a new institutional, regulatory, and financing framework for access expansion in addition to providing financial support to various sub-components of the access expansion program.
To improve the operational efficiency of the electricity distribution system and increase the population s access to electricity.

title.narrative: ECG annual accounts receivable (excluding government agencies and departments and the Ghana Water Company Ltd) equivalent to numberof days of annual sales

comment.narrative: <p>The uncertainty on the part of customers arising from the difficulties surrounding the Private Sector Participation (PSP) is at the core of the still elevated level of ECG annual accounts receivable. This indicator has been trending upwards since 2020 due to the negative economic impacts of Covid 19 on customer’s ability to honor their obligations on time</p>

title.narrative: Annual ratio of ECG revenues over its costs

comment.narrative: <p> <strong>Not Achieved</strong>-Consumer tariffs were reduced between 17-30% while the generation cost remained the same, despite that forex losses and idle capacity were borne by the government.</p>

title.narrative: Average annual hours of unplanned power outages per consumer in ECG system

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>-The indicator significantly improved since the commencement of the GEDAP project due to increased system improvement activities (injections, load balancing, defects correction, vegetation control).</p>

title.narrative: Tonnes of CO2 Avoided through the adoption of Renewable Energy

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Largely exceeded-</strong>Several renewable energy projects were commissioned by the private sector (CO2 savings = Annual Emission factor for Ghana Grid (EF) x Annual Energy Generated from Renewable Energy Installations. Although no new renewable energy project was undertaken under GEDAP AF2, this indicator has seen some upward movement due to the continuous operation of the 5 mini grids installed under GEDAP 1.</p>

title.narrative: Electricity losses per year in the project area

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Not Achieved-</strong>While the technical losses target was exceeded, (9.84 percent against a target of 10.20), the non-technical losses target was largely missed, reaching 20.16 percent against a target of 9.80 percent.  Performance for technicallosses results arose from the implementation of other electrification projects by other donors & ECG’s IGF.</p>

<p><strong>Electricity losses per year in the project area- Technical:</strong>  <strong>Not Achieved-</strong> Although the data shows that the metering activities under GEDAP AF2 has significantly improved ECG’s revenues in the project areas, this indicator has been trending upwards since 2020 due to COVID 19 restrictions on monitoring of customer residences and businesses to minimize power theft. This indicator has improved due to investments in the distribution network due to GEDAP and other interventions such as AfDB funded the Electricity Distribution System Reinforcement and Expansion Project, LV Network intensification, Bulk SupplyPoints and Primary Substations and ECG’s self-funded primary substations.</p>

<p><strong>Electricity losses per year in the project area- Non-Technical: </strong><strong>Not Achieved-</strong> Overall electricity losses worsened from a baseline of 26 percent in 2010 to a level of about 30 percent, missing the target. While the technical losses target was exceeded, (9.84 percent against a target of 10.20), the non-technical losses target was largely missed, reaching 20.16 percent against a target of 9.80 percent. Challenges to achieve the non-technical losses target were consecutive to the billing challenges on the implementation of the CMSsystem, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.???????</p>

<p><strong>Partially Achieved</strong>.  This indicator is a measure of the total revenue collected compared to the product ofthe total energy made available and the average end user tariff. It can be noted from the above that this indicator had increased to 80.61% by June 2020. However, due to Covid-19 Government relief and related restrictions on bill collection, the indicator has been trending downwards to 66.25% as at December 2021.</p>

title.narrative: Billed revenue (GWh) in the targeted consumer segments (above 600 units/month)

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Partially achieved</strong>-This indicator was 80% achieved. The end target was not achieved as the anticipated growth of demand by large customers was hampered by the slowdown of businesses because of Covid-19.</p>
<p>???????</p>

<p><strong>Largely Exceeded:</strong> The estimate of direct project beneficiaries was arrived at by multiplying by 6, which is the assumed number of persons by household in Ghana, the number of estimated grid (338,966) and no grid connections (22,892), and addin members of connected communities (65,000). Changes and opportunities arising from electricity services that affected the connected households affected the female members in the same way and proportion.</p>
